rows.description: Teasing among friends can be affectionate when both laugh and the topic is safe, and hurtful when it targets a sore spot or continues after distress. Stop and check in when the other person goes quiet or looks upset.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: amusement, affection, trust, hurt

rows.description: A school-age child enjoys puns, riddles and wordplay based on double meanings. Such humour signals growing language awareness and a wish to share fun and be part of the group.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child learns idioms such as "break the ice" or "raining cats and dogs". Children may take these literally at first, and cultural idioms in a second language need explanation.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Simile and metaphor in writing and speech [Expressing]
rows.description: A child writes "The moon is a silver coin" or "as quiet as a mouse". Figurative language shows imagination and helps express feelings that lack direct words.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child joins devotional songs, chants or hymns in a group. Rhythm and shared voice can bring calm, joy and belonging, and the experience does not need to be identical across children.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: joy, calm, nostalgia

rows.description: A child observes a family mourning through prayers, silence, rites or gatherings, and asks what death means. Simple honest explanations help, and children may grieve in short bursts and play between sadness.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age signer fingerspells names or unfamiliar words and uses name signs given by the community. Fingerspelling is a tool within a full language, not the language itself.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A signer gets attention by waving, tapping a shoulder or flicking lights, and keeps eye gaze on the signer. Looking at the speaker's hands and face is respectful and required, not rude.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A school-age child writes notes to friends, thank-you letters and a diary about the day. Writing lets a child share feelings that are hard to say aloud, and a diary needs privacy respected.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child writes stories with dialogue and short poems about feelings or pets. Fiction can carry real feelings, but a story is not proof that events or wishes are literal.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26
